Wesleyan Studies

  • Home
  •     Academics
  •     Wesleyan Studies

June 7 – July 1, 2027

Asbury Theological Seminary and Asbury University will be holding a Wesleyan Studies Summer Seminar (WSSS) in June 2027. This seminar has been established to develop and support research, writing, and publication in the broad field of Wesleyan studies. Drs. Tom McCall and Ken Collins will convene the seminar.

Designed for those working on articles, dissertations, and book-length manuscripts in the field of Wesleyan studies with an eye toward publication, the WSSS will take place June 7–July 1, 2027, on the Asbury Seminary Kentucky campus, with sessions held on Monday and Thursday afternoons.

All applications are heartily welcomed, even from those who have attended the seminar before. The program seeks to assemble the best class around the table for the richest conversation possible.

Benefits of Wesleyan Studies Seminar

  • Researchers become part of a community dedicated to their interests
  • No tuition fees
  • Access to the B. L. Fisher and Kinlaw Libraries, as well as to the special collection holdings in Wesleyan and Methodist studies
  • Free lodging and daily breakfast
  • Scholarships available for the airfare of international researchers
  • Complimentary evening meal on the days that the Seminar meets

Application Requirements

  • Application
  • Full vitae
  • Research description and plan for publication
  • Research project that addresses an aspect of the Wesleyan tradition and makes a generous contribution to the scholarly community
  • Priority is given to applicants who can attend the entire Seminar.
  • Applications must be received by January 15, 2027. Applicants will be notified of their acceptance by March 12, 2027.
